overview: Three 1940-42 List of Papers sheets index intercepted or misdelivered Japanese diplomatic messages, coded traffic from Southeast Asia and Latin America, Japanese crisis contingency instructions, and failed publisher and congressional efforts to republish Herbert Yardley's 'The American Black Chamber,' blocked as contrary to national-defense interests.

subfiles.title: List of Papers, items 41–43: Pocket Books and Yardley’s memoir
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / archival index sheet
subfiles.about: An index sheet records June 1940 correspondence with Pocket Books concerning the proposed republication of Herbert O. Yardley’s book.
subfiles.summary: Pocket Books' de Graff sought the 1933 codes-secrecy law's text, then dropped plans to republish Yardley's book after State objected.

subfiles.title: List of Papers, page 6, items 44–53: intercepted codes and republication request
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / archival index sheet
subfiles.about: This index page lists records on Japanese coded communications and the Bobbs-Merrill Company’s effort to republish “The American Black Chamber.”
subfiles.summary: Entries cover intercepted Japanese messages at Bandung and Bogotá, a crisis-instruction intercept, Bobbs-Merrill and Ludlow asking to republish Yardley's book.

subfiles.title: List of Papers, items 54–58: code studies, radio intercepts, and Chungking source
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / archival index sheet
subfiles.about: An index sheet records 1942 interdepartmental code-intelligence exchanges, the final rejection of Bobbs-Merrill’s request, and information from a Korean officer supplying Japanese messages.
subfiles.summary: Justice sought Japanese code messages and intercepts; a Chungking officer supplied code messages; Yardley republication deemed contrary to defense interests.

interest: Shows WWII-era Japanese code intercepts across Asia and Latin America, and the suppressed Yardley cryptography memoir republication bid.
